clue.text: I can't be bothered with calling head

parts.note: "Blow it!" or "blow that" is a weary dismissal, so blow stands for not being bothered
a calling is one's job or profession

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a call from the boss with a lazy 'can't be bothered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Head is slang for oral sex, which this compound names more bluntly.

clue.text: City tits taking Daily Express leader to heart

indicators.note: taking means the bosom word takes in the cleaner and the leader letter
to heart says the taken-in letters go right into the middle of the bosom word

parts.note: tits is slang for breasts, which make up a bust
a daily is a British cleaning woman, also called a char

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of Express is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Express

explanation.surface: A city newspaper's busty pin-up page is championed by the Daily Express editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Daily Express reads as the newspaper, but Daily is a cleaner and Express gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Head removed from piss-artist ace for Salome, possibly

indicators.note: removing the head means the first letter of the drinker's word is dropped

parts.note: a piss-artist is British slang for a heavy drinker, a toper
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A drunk is beheaded, much as John the Baptist was for Salome.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheading picks up Salome's story, but Salome is the Strauss work, so the definition carries a 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is a one-act stage work by Richard Strauss, so it is an example of this musical drama.

clue.text: God, Jack's got high on sex with Brenda!

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack; the 's means has
being high is being up
it is a coy word for sex
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, and ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A shocked exclamation at a sailor getting stoned and sleeping with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: God looks like an oath; it is the definition. Private Eye calls Queen Elizabeth II Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter was the chief of the Roman deities.

clue.text: Could easily make you go down, the fruity thing

definitions.text: Could easily make you go down, the fruity thing

parts.words: Could easily make you go down, the fruity thing
parts.note: the discarded skin of a fruit is the classic slapstick cause of a fall; go down also hints at oral sex

explanation.walkthrough: Go down plays on a smutty sense, but the thing is the slippery peel that trips people in cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: The peel of this yellow fruit is the comic-strip cause of slipping over.

clue.text: Shag sheep on date, glistening with sweat

parts.note: to bed someone is slang for having sex with them
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A farmyard scandal: a sexual encounter with a sheep on a dated night, leaving the culprit sweaty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedewed means covered in drops of moisture, as skin beaded with perspiration is.

clue.text: On-screen activity is bloody cheek

parts.note: B is the printed stand-in for a swear word such as bloody, as in 'b-- awful'
lip is cheeky backchat

explanation.surface: A complaint that what goes on on screen is sheer impertinence.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a spot of light on a radar screen marking a detected object.

clue.text: Balls-up of continental cable broadcast

parts.note: de is the French for of

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the wire word are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A European cable television broadcast goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls-up is British slang for a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a complete fiasco, which is what a balls-up is.

clue.text: Humour coarse, stupid person embracing royal . campaign of persecution

parts.note: wit is humour

indicators.note: embracing means the insult wraps around the royal letters

parts.note: the coarse insult for a stupid person, as the clue's word coarse warns
HH stands for His or Her Highness, a royal style

explanation.surface: A crude comedian's joke about a royal idiot turns into a hounding.
explanation.walkthrough: Coarse is the warning that the stupid person is the crude four-letter insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch-hunt is an organised hounding of people, named after historic trials for witchcraft.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom coupled with himself, going round bend — that's cereal produce for you

indicators.note: going round means the percussion word surrounds the letter for a bend

parts.note: tom paired with itself gives tom-tom, a kind of drum
a U-bend, so U is a bend

explanation.surface: A tomcat mating with himself goes round the bend, bizarrely producing cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is a hard wheat grown for pasta and semolina, a grain crop.

clue.text: Native American takes penis's first inch

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada and the northern plains

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word penis's

parts.note: the first letter of penis's

explanation.surface: A smutty image of a Native American measuring up an inch of anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch looks like a unit of length, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch along is to move slowly and stealthily, the same as to creep.

clue.text: Worried type, Brad wants nipper

parts.note: a brad is a small thin nail
something that nips is a biter

explanation.surface: An anxious Brad (Pitt, perhaps) wants a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad reads as a first name and nipper as a child; they are really a small nail and something that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biter is an anxious person, from the nervous habit of chewing the fingernails.

clue.text: Some old ditherer dressed as Dan Dare makes a sarcastically welcome comparison

parts.note: an old fart is a fussy, dithering old person, so some old ditherer is a fart
Dan Dare is a British comic-strip space pilot, so dressed as him is wearing spacegear

explanation.surface: A doddery old man dressed up as a comic-book space hero makes an unflattering comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was the space-pilot hero of the British comic The Eagle. The phrase completes the saying 'as welcome as' this.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'as welcome as a fart in a spacesuit' is a mocking simile for something nobody wants.

clue.text: The philosopher, John-Thomas not caught with joint

indicators.note: not here tells us the letter for caught is to be left out of the word

parts.note: John Thomas is British slang for the penis, as is cock
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a ham is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A rude description of a philosopher whose member went uncaught while he held a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Ockham was the medieval thinker behind Ockham's razor.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Ockham was an English medieval scholastic thinker, so he is a philosopher.

clue.text: "Stuff the French!" Sun's chief journalist entered disorderly

indicators.note: entered means the newspaper letter and reporter go inside the other words

parts.note: to ram is to cram or stuff
le is the French for the

indicators.note: chief means only the first letter of Sun's

parts.note: the first letter of Sun's
a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: A Sun reporter barges in shouting a jingoistic insult at the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff the French!' was a Sun-style headline, but here Stuff and the French are separate pieces wrapping the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramshackle means rickety and in disarray, a synonym of disorderly.

clue.text: Hack with tabloid turned dramatist

parts.note: a hack is a journalist; ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

indicators.note: turned means the newspaper word is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper such as a tabloid

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist abandons Fleet Street to write plays.
explanation.walkthrough: David Edgar is a British playwright, best known for adapting Nicholas Nickleby for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: David Edgar is a living English playwright, so the surname names a dramatist.

clue.text: Dreary Brenda: pointless, twisted and wrinkly

parts.note: grey means dull and dreary

indicators.note: twisted means the remaining letters are wrung into a new order
pointless means a compass-point letter, here north, is taken out of the name

explanation.surface: A sour picture of the Queen as dull, aimless, bent and old.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, but here the name is simply raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkly is slang for an old person, and an old man with a grey beard is the classic one.

clue.text: See 11
Peak division within two years for this far from popular political bunch?

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, a peak

indicators.note: within means the division word sits between the two year letters

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two years are two Ys
a part is a division

explanation.surface: A mountain-splitting quiz about which party has been unpopular for two years.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives were deeply unpopular after their 1997 defeat, around when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservatives, out of office and unloved at the time, were the political group far from popular.

clue.text: Runs out of articles — leaves

parts.note: the definite article THE, made plural with an S
to quit is to leave, so quits means leaves

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper runs out of stock and walks away.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs looks like a verb, but it is the noun for diarrhoea; 'the squits' is British slang for the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The runs is slang for diarrhoea, and the squits is another informal British name for it.

clue.text: Flush shown by Queen on getting wrong sort of IUD inserted

indicators.note: inserted means the rearranged device goes between the other two pieces

parts.note: Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen
a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: sort of means the contraceptive's letters are a rough version, rearranged

explanation.surface: The Queen blushes on being fitted with the wrong kind of contraceptive coil.
explanation.walkthrough: Flush looks like blushing; it means having plenty of money. An IUD is a contraceptive coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Quids in is British slang for being in profit, and flush means well supplied with cash.

clue.text: Cross-maker now dissatisfied with Blair?

parts.note: on a British ballot paper one marks a cross, so the maker of that cross is the person casting a ballot, here one fed up with the Prime Minister

explanation.walkthrough: Cross-maker suggests a carpenter of crucifixes; in Britain a ballot is marked with a cross. Tony Blair was Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts a cross on a ballot paper is a person casting a ballot in an election.

clue.text: Crafty arrivals to Britain, Greek family first in limited visibility

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the shortened visibility

parts.note: visibility cut short to its first three letters

indicators.note: first puts the family word ahead of the Greek letter

parts.note: kin is family
G is the standard abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: Smugglers sneak a Greek family into Britain under cover of fog.
explanation.walkthrough: Crafty means having boats, not cunning: the Norse raiders came by longship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse seafaring raiders who landed in Britain from the eighth century arrived by longship.

clue.text: One full of hackneyed opinions?

parts.note: a London taxi is formally a hackney carriage, and its driver is famous for opinions shared with passengers

explanation.walkthrough: Hackneyed seems to mean trite, but it hides the hackney carriage, the official name for a London taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A London taxi driver is stereotyped as forever sharing views, the opinions of the hackney trade.

clue.text: Class given by Chuck: "Getting head from escorts"

parts.note: to cast is to throw or chuck

indicators.note: head from means only the opening letter of escorts is taken

parts.note: the first letter of escorts

explanation.surface: A sex-education class given by a man called Chuck on oral sex from escorts.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting head reads as oral sex; it really means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Brown, pissed, puked and pissed

parts.note: to tan something is to brown it

indicators.note: pissed means drunk, so the letters of the next word stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A boozer's evening summed up: sunburnt, drunk, sick and drunk again.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two jobs: the first signals the shuffle, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanked up is British slang for very drunk, from filling up the tank.

clue.text: Nick died with vital erection

indicators.note: erection means something raised upright, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: live means vital or living

explanation.surface: A man dies with a vital part still standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a verb for stealing; Old Nick is a name for Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for Satan.

clue.text: Drink up second drink

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to sip is to drink

explanation.surface: Drink up, a second round is waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: Piss is slang for weak, poor beer, as in 'this lager is piss'; 'on the piss' means out drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Piss is crude British slang for alcohol, especially watery beer.

clue.text: Portable support for arse, base of member and shaft

parts.note: a member of parliament's base is the constituency, called a seat
a stick is a shaft of wood

explanation.surface: A rude anatomical description of something carried around to sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat-stick is a walking stick whose handle unfolds into a small perch, carried to racecourses and shoots.

clue.text: New woman joins right? I don't believe it!

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is the crossword's stock woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that a new woman has joined the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of disbelief 'Never!' means the same as 'I don't believe it!'

clue.text: Climaxes, points and rings the bell

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
to ding is to make a bell sound, so dings means rings the bell

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of orgasms scored like points in a game, with a bell rung each time.
explanation.definitionFit: Endings are the final climactic parts of a story, as a climax is.

clue.text: Goer composed song

parts.note: a composed person is calm and easy
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A composer has written a song called Goer.
explanation.walkthrough: Composed seems to be about writing music; it means calm. A goer is British slang for a sexually eager woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy lay and goer are both crude slang for a promiscuous person.
